Hypothetical. Someone says: "A limit only applies after I have decided it does." Which response is correct?

options.text: Correct. I decide on the day whether it applies
Wrong. The limits are written in the plan before trading, so they apply without a new decision
A limit is only a suggestion when the setup looks strong
A limit applies only in months when I am losing

explanations.a: A limit that waits for a new decision can be dropped on a bad day. That is why it is written in advance.
explanations.c: A setup that looks strong does not switch off a limit. The limit applies to every setup.
explanations.d: The limit applies in every month. Its purpose is to stop a bad run from growing.

prompt: Hypothetical. You say: "I should increase my size to recover before a cut." Which response is correct?

options.text: Correct, because a bigger size gets back faster
Wrong. A written cut in size reduces the damage while you review
Correct, after two losses
Correct, but only in strong markets

explanations.a: A bigger size makes each loss larger. It does not get back faster in any reliable way.
explanations.c: Two losses do not change the rule. A bigger size after losses breaks the plan.
explanations.d: Market conditions do not change the rule. The cut is a written step, and size does not grow after a loss.

prompt: Hypothetical. You say: "I can restart the next morning if I feel calm." Which response is correct?

options.text: Correct, because feeling calm is enough
Wrong. Restart needs a written review and the waiting period set in the plan
Correct, after any win
Correct, because the limit is just a guide

explanations.a: Feeling calm can change in an hour. The restart rule needs a review and a fixed waiting period.
explanations.c: A win does not prove the cause is fixed. The restart still needs the written review.
explanations.d: A limit is a rule, not a guide. It applies until the restart conditions are met.

prompt: Hypothetical. On the last trading day of the month, your losses reach your monthly limit of Rs 3,000 at the close. What fits the plan?

options.text: The limit does not count, because the month ends today
The limit counts. Record the breach and follow the suspension rule until the review
Trade on the first day of next month as if nothing happened
Trade more on the last day to end the month even

explanations.a: The limit applies to the losses in the month, including the last day. A breach on the last day still counts.
explanations.c: The suspension rule still applies. Starting the next month without a review skips the restart conditions.
explanations.d: Trading more after a limit breach breaks the rule. It can make the loss much bigger.

prompt: Hypothetical plan line: "Stop when things feel bad." Which part of this line is the mistake?

options.text: Having a stop at all
"Feel bad" is a feeling, not a yes or no test that the plan can check
Stopping
Nothing is wrong with the line

explanations.a: A stop is part of the method. The mistake is the test used to trigger it.
explanations.c: Stopping is the right action in the right case. The mistake is that the trigger cannot be checked.
explanations.d: The line fails because the trigger is a feeling. It cannot be checked before the moment you need it.
